annotations.text:
The same 21 days, the same blocks, both ways.

LEFT — time runs left to right, lanes are rows. The calendar convention. Today sits at the right edge, where a graph grows.

RIGHT — time runs top to bottom, lanes are rails. The git log convention. Today sits at the top, under your thumb, and the past is one scroll away. Weekends band for free, which the horizontal version cannot do legibly.

Both are 393 x 873, the Galaxy A52's viewport. The vertical one gives each day 25px of room instead of 17px, and it can keep going down for as long as you have history.

The payoff view. 52 columns, one per week, five lanes.

The thing to judge: BODY going quiet from March to November. Nothing in the app mentions it — the shape just says so. If that doesn't land at a glance, the encoding is wrong, not the concept.

Decided: B FULL / FADED for the day mark, 1 STACKED for the week cell.

That also makes the two resolutions speak one language — fill means enlarged, fade means diminished, at both zoom levels. Under solid/hollow they were two different languages, which was a bug nobody had named yet.

The rejected options stay on the board with their costs, so the choice keeps its reasons.
